text.en: Close your eyes for a minute and listen. The wind, the birds, a far-away vehicle: are they telling you something? In this story by Kamala Nair, a girl who longs to go to school finds that a river can be a very good friend and a wise adviser.

The chapter asks you to listen quietly to the sounds around you and think whether things around you listen to you too. Then it introduces Jahnavi, a bright girl in a coastal village in India. Her parents work on a farm, and she has a dream. You guess what it could be, how it can come true, and what your own dream is.
Jahnavi is crying by the river when a kingfisher, a green lizard and a bamboo thicket are all around her. Suddenly a sleepy, murmuring voice asks what is the matter. She is startled, because she thought she was alone. It is not the lizard, the kingfisher or the parrots, which shriek. The voice is the River itself, who says she has been coming to visit almost every day. Jahnavi tells the River that her family will not let her go to school like her brothers Ettan, whose real name is Gopi, and Meena. Her mother always says she is too small, maybe later. When she was five, little Ramu was born and she had to mind him. Now she is nearly ten and minds Little Appu, the youngest. She is scared of school and feels she is too old. She is full of whys: why spiders are yellow in yellow flowers, why bamboo trees rustle, why the moon always rises behind the hills, why baby fish become frogs. The River says she is making it breathless, and tells her that the moon goes down to the sea, like the River.
Jahnavi says even little Ramu goes to school. The River says it is a pity the school is not by the sea, because it could carry her, though she would get her feet wet. It tells her that little girls can do as much as little boys, and that she can slip into the school one morning, sit and listen, and maybe the teacher will let her stay. Jahnavi says she could not because she would be scared and chased out. The River laughs and reminds her she is not scared of the lizard, the snake in the bamboo clump or the trains rattling past the bridge. She asks about ships. The River says ships are big boats that carry hundreds of people along the sea with lights shining all night. They will not come up the river because they are too large. Chandu's catamaran is good enough for the River. The River ends with a message: try going to school first, and remember that it is up to you.
The next day Jahnavi gathers courage and reaches the school, breathless. She stands by the door while the teacher reads a story about a prince called Ashoka who became a great king. With Little Appu asleep on her shoulder, she creeps nearer and sits in the back row on the earthen floor. The teacher asks who she is, and the boys say she is Gopi's sister. The teacher says that if she really wants to come to school, they will talk to her father and find a way. Jahnavi tells her mother she will become a teacher and teach all the little girls in the village. She runs to tell the River, saying that she was scared but did it. She will learn to write her name, do sums, and find out why fish in the rice fields turn into frogs. The River chuckles and promises to tell her about ships.
The River is a character. Jahnavi's questions and the River's answers form two columns in the book: the moon's path, girls doing as much as boys, what ships are, and whether ships will come. The River's tone is assuring, and it is affectionate, kind-hearted and thoughtful. When it says slip along, it means move quietly. The line I couldn't repeated shows Jahnavi's fear. The writer describes nature in detail to set a peaceful scene and show Jahnavi's closeness to it. The conversation between a girl and a river makes the story lively and appealing. The main message is that courage and determination can make dreams come true, and that girls and boys have equal abilities.
River begins with a capital letter although it is a common noun, because the writer gives it human qualities, a voice and feelings. This is personification. Sound words in the text include shrieked, splashed, murmuring, wailed, rustle, gasped and rattling. Make them work in sentences, for example the leaves rustle or the train was rattling over the bridge. The word catamaran comes from Tamil kattu maram, meaning tied wood. Several English words were borrowed from Indian languages: karma and guru from Sanskrit, and sahib, chutney, verandah, jungle, areca and palanquin from other Indian languages. Find out the language of each from a dictionary. Prepositions show the relationship between nouns and other words. In the school paragraph the right choices are at school, outside the gate, inside the classroom, between two classmates, about numbers and excited about the adventure.

problem.en: Match each sound word with its meaning: shrieked, murmuring.

text.en: Read the meanings in the list.

why.en: Shrieked is made a high-pitched piercing sound, and murmuring is speaking in a low voice.

text.en: Use them in a sentence.

why.en: The parrots shrieked, but the River spoke in a sleepy, murmuring voice.

problem.en: Fill in the preposition: Jahnavi stood nervously ___ the gate (in/outside/above).

text.en: Think of where she stood before entering.

why.en: She did not go in yet.

text.en: Choose outside.

prompt.en: Retell the story in your own words and say what it teaches.

requiredIdeas.en: Jahnavi longs to go to school but is told she is too small and busy with her brothers.
The River encourages her and says it is up to her.
She goes to the school, listens, and the teacher agrees to help her stay.
The story teaches courage and that girls can do as much as boys.

commonMisconceptions.en: The River takes Jahnavi to the school in a ship.
Jahnavi's mother takes her to school on the first day.

points.en: The River gives Jahnavi courage to go to school.
Personification gives the River a voice and feelings, so River begins with a capital letter.
The story shows that girls can do as much as boys.
Sound words and prepositions make writing vivid and clear.
Catamaran comes from Tamil kattu maram, tied wood.
